samples.summary: Operator-facing self-hosting doc never mentions the new GOOGLE_* variables or Google OAuth app setup
samples.evidence: self-hosting.md is the canonical operator doc: it has a "Required" env table (lines 125-143), a "Miscellaneous"/optional env section, and a "GitHub OAuth Setup" walkthrough (line 431). The change adds three deployment-configured variables (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/CALLBACK_URL) whose whole point is that they are set per install, yet they are documented only in packages/backend/README.md and docs/design/backend.md. A self-hoster following this page has no way to learn the feature exists or that GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL is mandatory when the other two are set. Cost stays in docs, hence minor.
searchedFor: grep GOOGLE_ across repo (22 files, none under packages/documentation)
grep GITHUB_CLIENT_ID across repo (7 files incl. self-hosting.md)
read self-hosting.md env tables and 'GitHub OAuth Setup' section

samples.summary: Refactor unified the state helpers but left the two callbacks asymmetric: GitHub still upserts the user before validating state, Google validates first
samples.evidence: googleAuthCallback checks `consumeWebOAuthState` *before* `findOrCreateUser`, and both the code comment and docs/design/backend.md advertise "a refused callback leaves no user row (and no workspace) behind". githubAuthCallback (auth.controller.ts:126) still calls findOrCreateUser at the top, before the state checks at 155-166, so the same refused-callback scenario does create a row/workspace on the GitHub route. The stated refactor goal ('both providers run the same check rather than a copy of it', todo line 40-43) is only half realised, and the design doc now describes one property for one provider and not the other.

samples.summary: oauth-state.ts doc comments still describe the state as GitHub-specific after it became provider-shared
samples.evidence: Module comments say "its SHA-256 goes to GitHub as `state`" (line 11-13), `WebOAuthState.state` is documented as "Goes to GitHub as `state`" (line 161), and oauthStateCookieOptions' SameSite comment reasons about "GitHub redirects the browser back to us" (line 191). The new web-oauth-login.ts correctly generalises this, but its dependency's prose now names only one of two providers.

samples.summary: isSecureCookie() derives the deployment's public scheme only from GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL; GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL is ignored
samples.evidence: With the second provider added, GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL is an equally authoritative statement of the server's public scheme, but the cookie-secure decision (lines 229-240) still consults COOKIE_SECURE, then GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL, then NODE_ENV. In practice GitHub is mandatory so this rarely bites, but the new configuration surface was not folded into the single place that answers 'what scheme am I on'.

samples.summary: Unrelated devDependency reordering (playwright) bundled into the Google OAuth change
samples.evidence: The diff removes `"playwright": "^1.58.2"` from the end of devDependencies and re-adds it alphabetically. Harmless, but it is churn unrelated to the issue's outcome.
